attachments.text:
Kantonspolizei Zürich – Polizeiposten Wädenswil
Police report (Polizeirapport)

File no.: KAPO-ZH 26-01-3375
Complaint made: 31.01.2026, 12:05, at the Wädenswil police post
Complainant: Ruth Gerber, Bahnhofstrasse 137, Wädenswil

Facts as stated: On 31.01.2026 between approx. 09:45 and 10:00 the complainant left her flat for a short errand and closed the door without locking it. On her return she found that a handbag (with keys, wallet and a letter) had been taken from the hall and a jewellery box from the bedroom. The door showed no damage.

The complainant requests a criminal investigation and files a criminal complaint. Investigation opened.

Polizeiposten Wädenswil

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents at the insured location (the Versicherungsort of the policy) were stolen or damaged by a burglary, a robbery or a simple theft (including vandalism), even if nothing was taken?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the file state that the theft or damage was caused by a person who lived in the same household as the policyholder at the time?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim include costs, caused by the theft, of changing or replacing keys, magnetic cards or locks at the location named in the policy, or at a bank safe the policyholder rents?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the theft a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery), and so not a simple theft?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

text:
Dear Ms Morgan,

first, so there's no misunderstanding: nothing in my flat has been cleaned up, repaired or changed since the theft. The police officer who came on 31 January told me to leave things as they were, and I have.

I'm attaching the police report and the purchase records for the stolen things with what I paid for them.

Nobody broke in, and that's what makes me so cross with myself. On Saturday 31 January, a little before ten in the morning, I ran down to the bakery at the corner and pulled the flat door shut behind me without locking it, as I sometimes do for a quick errand. I was gone perhaps a quarter of an hour. When I came back the door was just as I'd left it, closed but unlocked, and my handbag was gone from the hall, and so was my jewellery box from the bedroom shelf.

Nothing about it was urgent from my side. I phoned you on Monday 2 February, you told me I could go ahead with new locks, and only after that did I book the locksmith.

My keys were in the handbag, together with a letter with my address on it. So the locksmith replaced the cylinders of my flat door and my letterbox on 4 February, with new keys. That cost CHF 2,280, and I'd like this to be part of my claim, together with the stolen things.

All of this happened at home, in my flat at Bahnhofstrasse 137 in Wädenswil, which I rent from Erlenhof Holdings. The stolen items come to CHF 8,100.

Thank you for your help so far.

Yours sincerely,
Ruth Gerber
